schema_grounding_notes: pathway vs disease MUTUAL EXCLUSION: pathway_name and disease_name must NEVER both be 'requested' — they are separate tables. pathway/signaling/KEGG/gene set → pathway_name only. disease/indication/disorder/condition → disease_name only. Mixing causes a cross-join explosion.

drug CLASS queries (TKI, kinase inhibitor, checkpoint inhibitor, etc.): when a query asks for drugs of a specific CLASS, the class definition becomes FILTER values — NOT 'requested' outputs. E.g. 'List TKIs' → drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target: ['Inhibitor'], target_name: ['tyrosine kinase'] as filters, drug_name: 'requested' as output. Do NOT mark drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target or target_name as 'requested' when they define the class being queried.

approval_status co-output rule: approval_status is ALWAYS a co-output column alongside disease_name when the join path includes drug_disease_association (i.e., whenever disease_name is a SELECT output from a drug→disease or disease→drug query). This enables clinical-maturity ranking (sort_order: Approved first, Discontinued/Withdrawn last). Omit it only for pure gene→disease or biomarker→disease queries that do NOT involve drug_disease_association.

approval_status: controlled vocabulary of development stages — Approved family (Approved, Approved in EU, Approved in China, Approved (orphan drug), Registered), submission family (NDA filed, BLA submitted, IND submitted, Application submitted, Approval submitted, Preregistration), Phase family (Phase 0, Phase 1, Phase 1/2, Phase 2, Phase 2/3, Phase 3, Phase 4, Clinical trial), discontinued family (Discontinued in Phase 1/2/3, Terminated, Withdrawn from market), and early family (Investigative, Preclinical, Patented). Map 'FDA approved'/'marketed' → Approved; 'clinical trial'/'in clinical trials' → 'Clinical trial' (lowercase 't' as stored on disk); map 'in trials' to the matching Phase value

drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target: maps free-text MoA to canonical TTD enum values; 'inhibitor' → Inhibitor, 'antagonist' → Antagonist, 'agonist' → Agonist, 'blocker' → Blocker (note: 'Antibody' is NOT a valid value in this column — TTD does not encode antibody modality in the MoA column)
gene_symbol: use HGNC official symbol only — p53→TP53, PD-1→PDCD1, PD-L1→CD274

target_name vs gene_symbol: target_name is the full protein name INCLUDING the gene symbol in parentheses as stored on disk (e.g. 'Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)'); gene_symbol is the short HGNC symbol (e.g. 'EGFR'); both columns exist on target_master_table — do NOT strip the parenthetical from target_name filters

brand/trade name lookup (Herceptin, Keytruda, Avastin, etc.) is resolved internally via trade_name_map → drug_name before querying; do NOT emit synonym as a filter field — drug_name is the correct output column

drug_crossmatching_association and target_uniprot_association are decoration tables (LEFT-joined) — ~40.3% of drugs (17,295/42,938, largely biologics) have no crossmatching row, so do not use chemical-identifier columns as a primary filter anchor

disease_name normalization: TTD uses canonical disease name strings that may differ from common usage (specific terminology, British spelling variants, specificity levels). Use medical knowledge to map user terms to their likely TTD-canonical forms; the entity resolver handles final fuzzy-matching, so an exact literal match is not required.

drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target interpretation: "Modulator" is TTD's broad catch-all for mechanisms not precisely curated. When the query is a mechanism-of-action question and TTD returns "Modulator", the synthesizer should supplement with pharmacological knowledge — for small-molecule enzyme/kinase drugs "Modulator" is functionally an Inhibitor; for monoclonal antibodies it is typically a Blocker or Antagonist. Always surface the TTD value plus the likely specific mechanism.

antibody target annotation: TTD may record either the molecular ligand OR the receptor as the primary target of an antibody drug — both refer to the same pharmacological pathway. Anti-ligand antibodies (e.g. anti-cytokine mAbs) bind the secreted peptide; anti-receptor antibodies bind the cell-surface receptor. When interpreting TTD target rows for antibody drugs, use pharmacological knowledge to clarify whether the annotated target is the ligand or its receptor.

drug_name FORBIDDEN in pure gene-disease and gene-pathway outputs: when the query asks ONLY for (gene ↔ disease) or (gene ↔ pathway) associations with no drug context, drug_name must be ABSENT from parsed_value — it is a JOIN KEY not an answer column. Exception: if the query explicitly asks about drugs alongside genes/diseases (e.g. 'which genes and drugs are linked to breast cancer?'), drug_name: 'requested' is correct. This rule does NOT block drug_name when drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target is present (that is a drug-target context, not a pure gene-disease context)

co_output_rules.reason: chemical identifiers are not interpretable without the drug name — if question names a specific drug emit drug_name: ["<name>"], otherwise emit drug_name: "requested"
UniProt xref and target type need the target name for context
bioactivity values need the target gene symbol for interpretation
mechanism of action needs the drug name, gene_symbol for context
approval status needs the drug name to be meaningful — if question names a specific drug emit drug_name: ["<name>"], otherwise emit drug_name: "requested"

drug-disease co-output: whenever drug_name is a SELECT output (disease→drug query), approval_status is always included — enables clinical-maturity sort_order (Approved first). Fires only when drug_name is in the output, not when it is a filter — so pure gene→disease and biomarker→disease paths are not affected.
protein name and gene symbol are companion identifiers for the same target — only when target_name is an OUTPUT (= "requested"), NOT when it is a filter value like ["tyrosine kinase"]

gene symbol and target name are companion identifiers on target_master_table — when gene_symbol is an OUTPUT, target_name must accompany it; only when gene_symbol is 'requested' (output intent), NOT when it is a filter like ["EGFR"]

few_shot_examples.question: List TKIs
few_shot_examples.note: drug CLASS query (TKI/checkpoint inhibitor/mAb): class keywords become FILTERS on MoA + target_name; drug_name is the output — never mark target_name as 'requested' when it defines the class

few_shot_examples.question: What drugs inhibit EGFR in TTD?
few_shot_examples.note: specific-target inhibitor query: gene_symbol + MoA as filters, drug_name as output

few_shot_examples.question: Which pathways is JAK2 involved in?
few_shot_examples.note: pathway query → pathway_name only. disease_name MUST be omitted — separate tables, mixing causes cross-join explosion

few_shot_examples.question: What biological processes involve EGFR?
few_shot_examples.note: 'biological processes' / 'signaling cascades' / 'KEGG' / 'gene sets' = pathway_name, NOT disease_name

few_shot_examples.question: Which diseases are associated with the APP gene?
few_shot_examples.note: disease query → disease_name only, pathway_name MUST be omitted; drug_name must also be ABSENT (it is a join key, not an output)

few_shot_examples.question: What conditions does CFTR mutation cause?
Which drugs are used to treat breast cancer?
few_shot_examples.note: disease→drug query — disease_name is the filter, drug_name + approval_status are co-outputs. approval_status is ALWAYS included alongside drug_name in drug-disease joins (enables clinical-maturity ranking — Approved first). Do NOT add gene_symbol or pathway_name unless explicitly requested.

few_shot_examples.question: What are the known targets of imatinib?
few_shot_examples.note: drug→target query: drug_name is the FILTER, target_name + gene_symbol are both output (co-output rule: target_name always travels with gene_symbol)

few_shot_examples.question: List FDA-approved drugs targeting VEGFR
few_shot_examples.note: VEGFR is a receptor FAMILY (KDR/FLT1/FLT4), NOT an HGNC gene symbol — use target_name: ["VEGFR"], not gene_symbol. 'FDA approved' → 'Approved'; drug_name is the output

few_shot_examples.question: What biomarkers are associated with breast cancer?
few_shot_examples.note: biomarker query → biomarker_name + disease_name as the output pair; NOT gene_symbol or drug_name

few_shot_examples.question: Which pathways does imatinib affect?
few_shot_examples.note: drug→pathway query: drug_name is the filter anchor, pathway_name is the output; do NOT add disease_name (separate table)

few_shot_examples.question: Which genes are associated with Alzheimer's disease?
few_shot_examples.note: pure disease→gene query: disease_name (filter) + gene_symbol (output) ONLY. drug_name MUST be absent — even if drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target appeared in nearby ANN columns, adding drug_name creates a 3-way cross-join explosion. This rule applies to all pure gene↔disease and gene↔pathway queries with no explicit drug context in the question.

few_shot_examples.question: What is the mechanism of action of imatinib?
few_shot_examples.note: mechanism-of-action query: drug is the FILTER, all three of gene_symbol + target_name + drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target are OUTPUT columns. Never omit drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target when the question explicitly asks about mechanism, pharmacology, or how a drug works.

few_shot_examples.question: Describe the mechanism of action of trastuzumab.
few_shot_examples.note: mechanism-of-action query for a biologic: same pattern as small molecules — drug is FILTER, gene_symbol + target_name + drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target are all OUTPUT. Do NOT add disease_name or approval_status unless the question explicitly asks for them.

few_shot_examples.question: what approved drugs targeting ALK treat lung cancer?
few_shot_examples.note: 'approved' is an ADJECTIVE restricting which drugs to return → approval_status: ['Approved'] as FILTER, NOT 'requested'. Co-output rule does NOT apply when the question constrains the approval stage. gene_symbol + disease_name are also filters; drug_name is the output.

few_shot_examples.question: Is the MAPK signaling pathway altered by imatinib?
few_shot_examples.note: NAMED PATHWAY + NAMED DRUG → both are FILTERS. The question names a specific pathway ('MAPK signaling') AND a specific drug ('imatinib') — both become filter lists. pathway_name is NOT 'requested' here. Contrast with 'which pathways does imatinib affect?' (no named pathway) → pathway_name: 'requested'.

few_shot_examples.question: cell cycle pathways involving CDK4
few_shot_examples.note: NAMED PATHWAY CATEGORY + NAMED GENE → both are FILTERS. 'cell cycle' is the pathway filter, CDK4 is the gene filter. CRITICAL: pathway_name is ['cell cycle'], NOT 'requested'.

few_shot_examples.question: PubChem CID of drugs used to treat tuberculosis
few_shot_examples.note: disease-drug PubChem query: no specific drug named → drug_name: 'requested' (output). disease_name is the filter. crossmatch_pubchem_cid is always 'requested' (ID output). CONTRAST with 'PubChem CID of aspirin' → drug_name: ['aspirin'] (filter, specific drug named).

_orchestrator_examples_comment: Few-shot examples for the orchestrator (disagreement resolver). Show correct output when one mapper hallucinates extra columns the question never requested.

orchestrator_examples.question: which diseases are associated with EGFR?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: drug_name not in query — it is a join-key intermediate in TTD's target→disease path, never an output when only gene + disease are asked. Reject mapper_2's extra column.

orchestrator_examples.question: what diseases does imatinib treat?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: drug→disease query. disease_name + approval_status are always co-outputs for drug-disease joins — approval_status enables clinical-maturity ranking (Approved first). MoA was NOT requested — mapper_2 hallucinated it. drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target belongs only when explicitly asked.

orchestrator_examples.question: what targets does gefitinib bind to?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: User asked for targets only. approval_status not in query — mapper_2 hallucinated it. approval_status is relevant only when the user asks about clinical status, approval, or phase.

orchestrator_examples.question: which drugs target VEGFR?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: VEGFR is a receptor family name (KDR/FLT1/FLT4), NOT an HGNC gene symbol — use target_name only. mapper_2 incorrectly set gene_symbol to the same family token, which is not a valid HGNC symbol and will return zero rows.

orchestrator_examples.question: which pathways does imatinib regulate?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: pathway_name and disease_name are mutually exclusive in TTD — they live in separate tables and mixing them causes a cross-join explosion. User asked for pathways only; omit disease_name entirely.

orchestrator_examples.question: which genes are linked to Alzheimer's disease?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: pure disease→gene query: output is gene_symbol ONLY. drug_name is NOT an output here — it is a join-key intermediate in TTD's disease→target path. mapper_2 hallucinated drug_name because drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target appeared in nearby ANN columns, but the question never asked about drugs. Adding drug_name would produce a 3-way cross-join explosion.

class_entity_rules: "TKI" expands to "tyrosine kinase inhibitor" — do NOT replace with a specific drug like imatinib
"checkpoint inhibitor" stays as-is — do NOT replace with pembrolizumab or nivolumab
"mAb" expands to "monoclonal antibody" — do NOT replace with a specific antibody

For named-gene inhibitor classes (e.g. "BRAF inhibitor", "PARP inhibitor", "CDK4/6 inhibitor", "EGFR inhibitor"): extract the gene symbol(s) from the class name using standard HGNC nomenclature, emit as gene_symbol filter, set drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target: ["Inhibitor"] as filter, and drug_name: "requested" as output — do NOT substitute specific drug names for the class

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Which pathways is DRD2 involved in?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: gene+pathway query: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on DRD2), pathway_name (SELECT output). drug_name and disease_name are IRRELEVANT — this is a pathway membership question, not drug or disease question.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Which KEGG pathways are associated with the BRAF gene?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: gene+pathway: gene_symbol + pathway_name are the core pair; target_name is a useful JOIN bridge. drug_name / disease_name / approval_status are irrelevant — do NOT include them.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Which diseases are associated with the EGFR gene?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: gene+disease query: gene_symbol (WHERE), disease_name (SELECT). drug_name is a JOIN-key intermediate NOT an answer column — MUST be dropped even if drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target appears in candidates.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What drugs inhibit EGFR?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: drug+target query: drug_name (SELECT output), gene_symbol + target_name (WHERE filter on EGFR), drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target (WHERE filter on Inhibitor). disease_name and pathway_name are irrelevant.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What are the approved drugs for breast cancer?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: drug+disease query: drug_name (SELECT), disease_name (WHERE filter), approval_status (WHERE filter). gene_symbol / pathway_name are irrelevant intermediate tables.

_comment: Schema rules for ttd. Injected into expander/filter/mapper prompts at runtime. GENERATED from dbs/ttd/schema.yaml by scripts/gen_schema.py — DO NOT EDIT.
db_description: Therapeutic Target Database — curated drug/target/disease/pathway associations with approval status, mechanism of action, synonyms, bioactivity data, and UniProt cross-references

column_notes_override.approval_status: TTD development-stage vocabulary — e.g. Approved | Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Phase 3 | Phase 1/2 | Investigative | Preclinical | Patented | Discontinued in Phase 2 | Terminated | Withdrawn from market; map 'FDA-approved'/'marketed' → Approved
column_notes_override.drug_name: individual drug name (INN or brand) — NOT drug class terms like TKI, mAb, checkpoint inhibitor, BRAF inhibitor; brand names are resolved to INN via trade_name_map before querying
column_notes_override.drug_mechanism_of_action_on_target: TTD MoA enum — e.g. Inhibitor, Agonist, Antagonist, Blocker, Activator, Modulator, Binder, Ligand; NOT free-text phrases
column_notes_override.compound_activity_gene_symbol: HGNC official symbol — p53→TP53, PD-1→PDCD1, PD-L1→CD274
column_notes_override.gene_symbol: HGNC official symbol — p53→TP53, PD-1→PDCD1, PD-L1→CD274
column_notes_override.target_type: TTD target development stage (long form in target_uniprot_association) — Successful target, Clinical trial target, Literature-reported target, Patented-recorded target, Discontinued target, Preclinical target
column_notes_override.uniprot_gene_symbol: HGNC official symbol — p53→TP53, PD-1→PDCD1, PD-L1→CD274
